info.title: FPA Results API
info.description:
Read-only API over the freestyle frisbee judging, results and rankings services.

Upstream is five independent microservices, each with its own store and no shared query
layer. This API fetches all of them, resolves duplicate player identities, normalizes
inconsistent division names, and joins ranking points back to the events that produced
them — then serves the result from an in-memory index.

**Freshness.** Data is refreshed on a tiered schedule rather than per request, so responses
can be up to an hour behind upstream. `GET /health` reports exactly how stale the data is.

**Data quality.** Upstream enforces no referential integrity. Records that reference a
missing player or event are kept and flagged (`unknown: true` on a team member, warnings
on `/health`) rather than dropped, so nothing disappears silently.

bearerAuth.description: Shared secret from REFRESH_TOKEN. Only used by POST /refresh.

divisionRaw.description: Exactly as stored upstream, before normalization

place.description: Finishing position in this pool. 1 is best. Sort and display by this.

points.description: Raw score as recorded, whose meaning DEPENDS ON THE RULESET the event used. Under FPA2020 scoring a higher number is better; under SimpleRanking it is a sum of judge ranks, so a LOWER number is better. The ruleset is not exposed in the results data, so points are not comparable across events — never sort or rank by this field. Use `place`.

unknown.description: True when this GUID is absent from the player directory

id.description: Canonical player GUID, shared across all upstream services

fpaWebsiteId.description: Id of this player on the legacy FPA website

aliasIds.description: Duplicate GUIDs that resolve to this player

rankings.description: Standings in points-based ranking series. Empty if unranked.

ratings.description: Standings in Elo-style rating series. Empty if unrated.

wins.description: First places across all rounds and pools

breakdown.description: Which events produced these points, highest first

rank.description: Positional — ratings carry no stored rank

matchCount.description: Head-to-head comparisons behind this rating; low counts are unreliable

confident.description: Near-certain match, but still requires confirmation

placementCount.description: Use as a tiebreaker: an active player is the likelier match

ready.description: False until the first successful load

builtAt.description: When the in-memory index was built

origin.description: Where the current data came from

warnings.description: Non-fatal data problems found while normalizing

get.summary: Get a player profile with career metrics
get.description: Returns the player, aggregate career stats, their current standing in every ranking and rating series, and every recorded placement (most recent first). An alias GUID is accepted; the response always carries the canonical id, so callers can detect the redirect and store the canonical value.

get.description: Ratings are an Elo-style strength estimate derived from head-to-head outcomes. They are NOT the same as rankings: rankings accumulate tournament points over a season, ratings estimate current strength and have no points breakdown. A rating backed by a low `matchCount` is statistically weak — surface that number alongside the rating rather than the rating alone.

get.description: Ratings are an Elo-style strength estimate derived from head-to-head outcomes. They are NOT the same as rankings: rankings accumulate tournament points over a season, ratings estimate current strength and have no points breakdown. A rating backed by a low `matchCount` is statistically weak — surface that number alongside the rating rather than the rating alone. Defaults to `rating-open`.

schema.description: Exclude players with fewer than this many head-to-head matches. Most rated players have very few, so a floor of 50-100 gives a far more meaningful leaderboard.

get.summary: List historical ranking and rating snapshots
get.description: Rankings and ratings are published upstream as dated snapshots. This lists them newest first; snapshots flagged hidden upstream are excluded. Use these to chart a player or division over time.

503.description: Data is still loading or upstream is unavailable

get.description: Fetched from upstream on demand rather than held in memory: there are around 100 snapshots and they are read rarely, so caching them all would cost a lot of memory for little gain. Expect this to be slower than the other endpoints. A snapshot contains either rankings or ratings depending on its key; the other array is empty.

get.summary: Find upstream events that may correspond to one of ours
get.description: Results are suggestions ranked by similarity, never an automatic link. fpa-events and the upstream services share no identifier, so a confident-looking match can still be the wrong year or a junior division. Always require human confirmation before storing the id.

get.summary: Find upstream players that may correspond to one of our users
get.description: Results are suggestions ranked by similarity, never an automatic link. fpa-events and the upstream services share no identifier, so a confident-looking match can still be the wrong year or a junior division. Always require human confirmation before storing the id. Names are especially unreliable here — several people in the directory share a name.

get.description: Reports per-source upstream health, when data was last refreshed, and any data-quality warnings. Returns 503 while the index is not yet ready, but the body is identical either way — this is the endpoint to read when something looks wrong.

503.description: Not ready — no data loaded yet

post.description: Pulls the full corpus now instead of waiting for the scheduled refresh. Intended to be called right after results are entered upstream. Requires a bearer token matching REFRESH_TOKEN; when that variable is unset the route is disabled rather than left open.

503.description: Refresh failed, or the endpoint is disabled
